the prior interreinforcement time length alone is insufficient to influence the subsequent IRT length, and that a temporal response patter arises when an IRT interacts with schedule contingences to control the inter-reinforcement interval.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of reinforcement on the control of response rate and interresponse times.
the role of reinforcement in the control of sequential interresponse time dependencies.
the temporal organization of behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of the interresponse time in the sequential interresponse time pattern is to provide a time base for the interaction between the interresponse and the interreinforcements.
reinforcement is a necessary but not sufficient condition in controlling sequential interresponse-time patterns.
the temporal response patterns are controlled by the interaction between the interresponse time and the interreinforcment time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reinforcement controls sequential interresponse time dependencies in a differential-reinforcement schedule.
the temporal pattern of responding is controlled by the interaction between interresponse time and the schedule of reinforcement.
the prior interreinforcement time is an important factor in the sequential response pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal structure of the response pattern is not determined simply by the temporal structure of interresponse times.
the interresponse time is not a sufficient condition for sequential dependencies.
the interresponse time is not a sufficient determinant of the subsequent interresponse interval.
